newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden keeping mum on EMU announcement timing.
newsitem.headline: Sweden keeping mum on EMU announcement timing.

text.p: Sweden was keeping quiet on Thursday on when its ruling party would reveal its position on Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU).
Prime Minister Goran Persson's office referred questions about when the country would give its opinion on EMU to the finance ministry.
But a spokeswoman for Finance Minister Erik Asbrink said she did not know any details about an announcement.
"I assume there will be a press conference, or some kind of meeting or seminar," the spokeswoman told Reuters.
Finance Minister Erik Asbrink earlier pledged to make Sweden's view of EMU membership clear in the next few weeks.
Asbrink's spokeswoman has said the minister would advise markets at least a few hours before he announces his decision.
Persson said on Wednesday an annoucement would be made on Friday or next week, but added that this was not definite and the statement could be even later.

The executive committee of Sweden's ruling Social Democratic Party, called the VU, which will recommend a view to the party congress in September, is scheduled to meet twice before a party meeting on June 23 and 24 in Skelleftea, Sweden.
The party view is expected to come out of one of these meetings, which are on May 29 and June 18. The meeting on Friday of the party committee will be held from 0800 to 1400 GMT.

The secretary in charge of organising the VU meeting said no news conference had been scheduled for Friday and EMU was actually not on the agenda for the meeting. However, this did not mean EMU could not be discussed, the secretary said.
"On the agenda for the meeting of the executive board there is no mention of EMU," Berith Andersson told Reuters.
"But it happens at almost every meeting that an issue is brought up by one of the members that was not on the agenda," she said.
"If there is a decision...they would have to announce a press conference at that moment. This happens all the time," she said.

The VU consists of Prime Minister Goran Persson, Foreign Minister Lena Hjelm-Wallen, Social Democratic Party secretary Ingela Thalen, former deputy Prime Minister Mona Sahlin, Parliamentary Party Chairman Sven Hulterstrom, Environment Minister Anne Lindh and Bertil Jonsson, head of the Swedish Trade Union Federation (LO).
Finance Minister Erik Asbrink attends the meetings but does not have voting rights.

Persson said this week he had formulated his personal opinion and that when the ruling Social Democrat party announces its stance on EMU it would be more than a simple yes or no answer and the view would have a majority support in parliament.
